$comment: Canonical framework patch set. pnpm only honors patchedDependencies at the app/workspace root, so these ship inside @octane-xplat/cli and downstream apps materialize them via `xplat patches apply` (copies files into <app>/patches/ + merges the yaml block). `pnpm sync:patches` generates the config package's patch files and the template config; `pnpm check:patches` fails on drift. Maintain a patch with `pnpm patch <specifier>` + `pnpm patch-commit` — the root workspace yaml points here so commit writes land in this dir. Entries with `template: false` target repo-internal environments (e.g. the windows preview matrix) and are omitted from the starter's patchedDependencies — pnpm fails install on declared-but-unused patches.

patches.why: Published 0.14.0 still requires renderer-owned Children.toArray/map with explicit universal-native re-exports for older runtimes, universal signal-read tracking and local hooks, root event-error forwarding, the complete universal imperative-ref lifecycle, the Descriptor declaring-owner reader fallback, and the signal-owner/enclosingOwner chain so child reads reuse instance declarations. Rebased against the registry 0.14.0 tarball, including local signal-hook registration in the split runtime/hooks modules. Provider null/undefined descendant cleanup is now upstream and no longer patched. Marks generic binding bags from bagOf so fragment commit rehomes their DOM parent references, preventing stale fragment parents, namespace recursion, and invalid insertion during typeahead updates. Preserves keyed component ownership through compiler-generated transparent root slots so native map reorders retain host identity, state, and portal content.
patches.dropWhen: An octane release exports universal Children normalization, integrates universal signal reads/local hooks and owner ancestry, forwards uncaught event-handler errors, and supports optional/replaced/nested imperative refs with callback cleanup. Generic binding bags must also participate in transaction-fragment parent rehoming. Universal array reconciliation must also preserve component keys through transparent root-slot wrappers.

patches.why: Published 9.1.3 ships the #11446 nested-tab-frame lifecycle fix and iOS explicit-size flex alignment, so those hunks are removed. Retains the unshipped parent-padding measure-spec fix and Android explicit-size flex alignment, iOS continuous corner clipping, CSS @layer cascade support, custom Android variable-font weight mapping, and percentage translate parsing, native view, and animation support. Verified against the registry 9.1.3 tarball; it has no Windows implementation, so the separate Windows preview patch remains.
patches.dropWhen: A published @nativescript/core release contains the remaining flexbox measure/alignment, continuous corners, cascade layers, custom Android variable-font weight mapping, and percentage-translate fixes (NativeScript/NativeScript#11481).

patches.why: @nativescript/vite serializes bundled CSS and dev app.css through reworkcss `css`@3.0.0, which mis-parses @layer into garbage selectors — rules die before reaching _populateRules. Adds atlayer() covering block and statement forms. Applies to a transitive dep — no app declares it directly.
patches.dropWhen: npm `css` is unmaintained — drop when @nativescript/vite's serializer stops using it (e.g. pointed at NS's vendored css/lib/parse; NativeScript#11462)

patches.why: Remaining dev-server fixes on @nativescript/vite 8.0.20: collect re-export specifiers in the .vite/deps rewrite; route outside-roots /@fs paths through /ns/m; probe non-active platform and native suffixes; redirect bare octane to octane/universal/native in deps-bundle esbuild passes; add .mobile to tsconfig-paths and generated checker suffixes; scan the app-local pnpm virtual store for served node_modules URLs; ignore per-package turbo.json as workspace markers; resolve # package-imports specifiers in served-module rewrites; preserve, compile, and hot-update virtual stylesheets (NativeScript#11551); and inspect ESM export declarations/specifiers for native default-import validation instead of matching comments, strings, or a narrow export syntax (NativeScript#11566). Shared-source graph and hot-context IDs now use the same app/workspace/@fs paths as served imports, preserving distinct roots (NativeScript#11569); extensionless workspace requests probe filesystem-anchored extension/platform candidates so hot reimports can fetch shared modules (NativeScript#11570). Linked-checkout discovery and candidate anchoring shipped in 8.0.20 (NativeScript#11559), so those local hunks are removed.
patches.dropWhen: Upstream ships the remaining re-export, outside-roots /@fs, platform/native candidate, deps-bundle alias, .mobile suffix (checker: NativeScript#11480), app-local pnpm store, turbo.json workspace-marker, # package-imports, virtual stylesheet fixes (NativeScript#11551), accurate default-export link validation (NativeScript#11566), and shared-source HMR identity preservation (NativeScript#11569), and extensionless workspace fetching (NativeScript#11570).

patches.why: Driver treats a prop dropped from an update's complete prop bag — or set to `undefined`/`null` — as a removal and restores the documented default: Property/CssProperty setters get `unsetValue`, plain fields restore the captured pre-prop value, and applied `style` keys diff per key. A never-applied `undefined` still skips the write since NativeScript native setters coerce it (e.g. editable → ios.userInteractionEnabled = NO). Aligns intrinsic ref types with Octane callback cleanup and nested arrays with optional entries. Advertises the implemented visibility capability so committed suspense bodies can be retained while pending. Preserves authored Grid row/col/span metadata independently of NativeScript defaults and computed auto-placement, notifying Grid when placement props change.
patches.dropWhen: @nativescript-community/octane ships removal-reset prop semantics, the undefined-skip, visibility capability, Octane-compatible intrinsic ref types, and Grid authored placement metadata with change notifications upstream.

patches.why: Retains the workspace's NativeScript driver fixes when upgrading to 0.2.5 for portal support: a prop dropped from an update's complete prop bag — or set to `undefined`/`null` — is a removal that restores the documented default (Property/CssProperty setters get `unsetValue`, plain fields the captured pre-prop value, `style` keys diff per key); a never-applied `undefined` still skips the write. Synced with PR #14: registered setters are identified before resetting (ordinary fields never receive the sentinel), inline removal refreshes matching class CSS through the isolated core 9.1 `_cssState.onChange` hook, CSS variables use public removal, strings use the core CSS parser, and replacement views capture fresh defaults. Also advertises the implemented visibility capability, carries Octane callback ref types, and preserves authored Grid row/col/span metadata. Hosts custom-layout containers (e.g. MasonKit ViewBase) that own child lists via insertChild/removeChild/getChildrenCount without subclassing LayoutBase. Additionally, the masonry cutover: masonview resolves to MasonKit View and scrollview to MasonKit Scroll as the only layout containers, with zero layout props — every former prop name warns-and-drops and all CSS semantics arrive through the style bag; foreign native leaves mirror resolved class and inline layout styles through Style.fromView, observe longhand changes and native recreation, and explicitly clear removed placement — removal restores the CSS cascade, so a later sibling attachment cannot resurrect removed tracks. Container alignment uses the core stretch default without a local style override, allowing class-authored centering. Inline style resets reapply the matching CSS cascade. Re-exports Octane's ClassValue unchanged and stringifies truthy numeric class values while omitting 0 and NaN, matching Octane 0.11. Maps collapsed foreign native leaves to Mason display:none, restoring effective display on visibility changes so both layout hosts omit the same item (#45).
patches.dropWhen: The upstream driver hosts Mason containers, preserves removal-reset semantics, and synchronizes resolved foreign-leaf layout styles with class/inline precedence and native-view lifecycle support. Foreign leaf visibility must also remove collapsed items from Mason layout and restore their effective display.

patches.why: octaneServerStrategy's SCRIPT_FILE_RE only covers [jt]sx? — .tsrx edits never emit the deferred ns:hmr-delta broadcast, so component HMR silently never reaches the device. Also counts open /ns-hmr sockets so the update summary stops reporting recipients=0 for delivered updates. Includes shared script sources in transaction ordering while excluding dependencies, tests and declarations. External-source edits use the absolute source for graph identity and a Vite /@fs transform URL instead of treating parent-relative paths as app URLs.
patches.dropWhen: vite-octane release adds .tsrx matching and uses canonical graph IDs with filesystem transform URLs for external sources

patches.why: apps/windows pins the @7d0adce pkg.pr.new preview based on @nativescript/vite 8.0.13, so its separate patch carries /ns/m re-export records, vendor-manifest gating for plugin-patterned packages, percent-decoding (the preview predates 8.0.17/#11483), and .mobile-aware tsconfig-paths probing.
patches.dropWhen: windows moves off the preview pin — the real fix lands upstream with the windows platform merge (NativeScript#11272/#11468)

patches.why: Windows spike: the shared-file subset of the 9.1.2 patch — @layer cascade machinery (css-tree parser, css-selector, style-scope), the #11446 frame/tab-view common fixes, and the flexbox common measure-spec — applied to the @7d0adce preview. iOS/Android impl-file hunks are dead code on windows and were dropped. Repairs Windows replacement-only pointer event registration with independently owned subscribers, ref-counted hover, unload/reload cleanup, cancellation/capture-loss handling, disabled guards, and separated tap/double/long-press delivery. Repairs parent-driven percentage sizing initialization, resize/reparent/load/unload ownership, and padded content-box updates. Restores Windows input focus/blur events and lifecycle ownership, IsEnabled forwarding, explicit accessible names, fail-closed secure readonly, and literal non-CSS property values. Published 9.1.3 has no Windows implementation files, so apps/windows intentionally retains the @7d0adce preview and this separate patch when mobile consumers upgrade to 9.1.3.
patches.dropWhen: upstream ships the fixes and windows moves off the preview pin (NativeScript#11462, #11446, core windows merge); pointer observer source fix is retained in .agents/patches/windows-pointer-core.patch until an upstream release contains it. Percentage sizing source fix is retained in .agents/patches/windows-layout/core-percent-source.patch until upstream includes it. Input source repair is retained in .agents/patches/windows-input-core.patch until upstream includes it.

patches.why: Enables `resolveHiddenExtensions` on the language plugin's typescript facet so extensionless specifiers (e.g. './Text') probe `.tsrx` after moduleSuffixes — required for a single extensionless shared barrel to resolve per-platform leaves under tsrx-tsc and the IDE plugin.
patches.dropWhen: @tsrx/typescript-plugin sets resolveHiddenExtensions in its typescript facet upstream

patches.why: linkifyjs declares /\p{L}/u and /\p{Emoji}/u as regex literals at module scope; NativeScript's embedded V8 builds without ICU, so the literals throw SyntaxError at parse time and poison the whole bundle (any bundled app importing @tiptap/extension-link dies on boot). Rewrites them as try/catch new RegExp builds with ASCII-range fallbacks — same behavior where ICU exists, graceful degradation where it doesn't.
patches.dropWhen: linkifyjs ships an ICU-free-compatible build, or the leaf stops pulling @tiptap/extension-link

patches.why: useEditor.ts reads bare process.env.NODE_ENV — no node global exists in the harness typecheck program. Adds a module-local process declaration for typecheck. (The './Context' self-import half of the 0.0.51 patch shipped upstream in 0.0.52 via octanejs/octane#1502.)
patches.dropWhen: @octanejs/tiptap declares process ambiently in useEditor.ts (closed unmerged upstream) or the leaf stops typechecking its raw sources

patches.why: @lexical/link declares a /\p{L}\p{N}/u URL matcher as a regex literal at module scope; NativeScript's embedded V8 builds without ICU, so the literal throws SyntaxError at parse time and poisons the whole bundle (any bundled app importing @lexical/link dies on boot). Same fix as linkifyjs: try/catch new RegExp with an ASCII-range fallback — the matcher only feeds autolink, which native doesn't use.
patches.dropWhen: upstream builds the URL matcher via new RegExp, or NS runtimes ship ICU

patches.why: @nativescript/doctor's Android runtime check reads the app's raw devDependencies specifier and npm dist-tag resolves anything that isn't a semver range — a pnpm `catalog:` pin throws 'The determined Android runtime version ... is not valid' and kills `ns build android` before toolchain checks. Resolve catalog specifiers through the installed package's manifest, reusing the existing tgz-branch mechanism.
patches.dropWhen: @nativescript/doctor resolves non-registry specifiers (catalog:, workspace:, link:) to the installed package version, or nativescript stops gating `ns build` on it.

patches.why: shaders@4.0.0 inlines TypeGPU 0.12.3 into dist/core/std-ClftfWpF.js, which declares /\p{XID_Start}/ and /\p{XID_Continue}/ regex literals at module scope (WGSL identifier validation, external prop-chain matching, minify separator check). NativeScript's embedded V8 on iOS (@nativescript/ios 9.1.0) and Android (@nativescript/android 9.1.1, V8 14.9.207.39) is built without ICU — every \p{…} escape is a SyntaxError, even in a never-called function, so a literal fails the whole module at parse time and any bundled app importing `shaders/js` dies on boot. Rewriting to \p{ID_Start}/\p{L} would not help — all property escapes are rejected. The patch builds the regexes via try/catch new RegExp with ASCII/non-ASCII-range fallbacks — byte-identical .source where ICU exists. dist/js/bundle.js, react/bundle.js, and cli.js carry the same escapes but are unreachable from `shaders/js` and left unpatched.
patches.dropWhen: TypeGPU ships ICU-free identifier regexes and a `shaders` release bundles that TypeGPU, or NativeScript runtimes ship ICU
